```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(jabotR)
```

This guide demonstrates how to use the `jabot_missing()` function in the `jabotR` package to find which species expected in a specific Brazilian region are still missing from a local herbarium — and where a collecting expedition could most easily find them.

## Function Overview

`jabot_missing()` identifies species listed in the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) that are expected to occur in a target Brazilian state and/or municipality (`geo`) but are absent from a given JABOT-hosted herbarium (`herbarium`), regardless of where in Brazil that herbarium's own specimens were collected. Unlike [`jabot_gaps()`](/articles/identify_jabot_gaps.qmd), which compares a herbarium against the whole of Brazil, `jabot_missing()` narrows the comparison to a specific region and searches the pooled occurrence records of the JABOT network (all herbaria, or a subset given by `network_herbaria`) for existing vouchers of the missing species collected within that region — helping prioritize where new collecting expeditions could target them.

The analysis includes summary statistics, a ranked table of missing species with known network vouchers and municipalities, missing species by family, an interactive map of candidate collecting localities, a municipality-level heat map ranking collecting priority, and a full record-level table of every individual network voucher — each linking out to the physical specimen (image/viewer page) when the source herbarium provides one.

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `herbarium` | Acronym of the target/local herbarium whose gaps are being assessed (e.g. `"HUEFS"`). |
| `geo` | One or more Brazilian state names/acronyms and/or municipality names delimiting the region of interest (e.g. `"Bahia"`, `"BA"`, or `c("Feira de Santana", "Ilhéus")`). |
| `network_herbaria` | Herbarium acronyms to restrict the pooled network sample used to search for candidate collecting points. `NULL` uses all JABOT-hosted herbaria. |
| `jabot_path` | Path to a directory with previously downloaded JABOT DwC-A files, shared by both the target herbarium and the network pool. `NULL` downloads automatically. |
| `format` | Static formats to save individual figures: `"pdf"`, `"png"`, or both. The HTML report is always generated regardless. |
| `fig_width`, `fig_height` | Dimensions (in inches) of saved figures. |
| `open_report` | If `TRUE`, opens the HTML report in the default browser after rendering. |
| `verbose` | If `TRUE`, prints progress messages. |
| `dir` | Output directory. Defaults to `"<herbarium>_missing_<geo>"`. |

## Basic Use Case

```{r}
missing_analysis <- jabot_missing(herbarium = "HUEFS",
                                  geo = "Bahia",
                                  verbose = TRUE,
                                  open_report = TRUE,
                                  dir = "HUEFS_missing_Bahia")
```

## Narrowing the Search to Specific Municipalities

FFB's state-level checklist is always resolved from the state(s) intersecting `geo`, while the candidate collecting map stays restricted to the municipalities supplied.

```{r}
missing_analysis <- jabot_missing(herbarium = "HUEFS",
                                  geo = c("Feira de Santana", "Ilhéus"),
                                  verbose = TRUE,
                                  open_report = TRUE)
```

## Restricting the Network Pool

By default, the pooled network sample includes all JABOT-hosted herbaria. `network_herbaria` restricts the candidate collecting-locality search to a specific subset, individual figures can be exported as PDF/PNG, and `jabot_path` reuses previously downloaded data.

```{r}
missing_analysis <- jabot_missing(herbarium = "HUEFS",
                                  geo = "Bahia",
                                  network_herbaria = c("ALCB", "CEPEC"),
                                  jabot_path = "jabot_download",
                                  format = "pdf",
                                  verbose = TRUE,
                                  open_report = TRUE)
```

## Example Output

The HTML report ranks municipalities by collecting priority and lists every individual network voucher of the missing species, each with a direct link to the physical specimen when available:

![Priority-municipality heat map in the `jabot_missing()` HTML report](/figures/jabot_missing_report_priority_map.png){.lightbox}

![Candidate collecting localities and full record-level voucher table](/figures/jabot_missing_report_records_table.png){.lightbox}

The function also returns (invisibly) a named list with every computed data frame:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
missing_analysis$n_missing
missing_analysis$pct_missing
head(missing_analysis$taxon_missing)
head(missing_analysis$municipality_priority)
```

## Tips

- Species with `locatable = TRUE` in `taxon_missing` already have a known network voucher in the region — these are usually the easiest targets for a first collecting trip.
- `missing_pool_records` lists every individual specimen (not aggregated by species); its `specimenLink` column links to the physical specimen image/viewer page whenever the source herbarium's Darwin Core Archive provides one.
- Downloading the full JABOT network (`network_herbaria = NULL`) can be slow on the first run — supply `jabot_path` afterwards, and consider restricting `network_herbaria` for quick, repeated exploration.
- For a nationwide (rather than region-scoped) version of the same collecting-priority idea, see `priority_map = TRUE` in [`jabot_gaps()`](/articles/identify_jabot_gaps.qmd).
